dimensions.assessment: Affects individual investors holding professional credentials, private companies offering unregistered securities, and the Securities and Exchange Commission.
dimensions.evidence: revises who may be considered an accredited investor for purposes of participating in private offerings of securities.

dimensions.assessment: Expands and formalizes pathways for individuals to qualify as accredited investors based on professional credentials rather than solely financial thresholds.
dimensions.evidence: allows the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) discretion in determining what certifications, designations, or credentials investors must possess

dimensions.assessment: The source material does not state direct federal spending or economic revenue effects.
Amends the Securities Act of 1933 and the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act to add regulatory review mandates and credential rules.
dimensions.evidence: To amend the Securities Act of 1933 and the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act with respect to the definition of accredited investor

dimensions.assessment: Establishes permanent regulatory authority accompanied by a recurring review requirement every five years.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than 18 months after the date of the enactment of this paragraph and not less frequently than once every 5 years thereafter, the Commission shall review

missing_information: The number of individuals who would newly qualify as accredited investors is not provided.
importance_detail.rationale: Allows the SEC discretion to include specific professional credentials and licenses for accredited investor status in private securities offerings and mandates periodic five-year reviews.
